sections.h2: Where is East Hartford and how is the town laid out?
sections.html:
East Hartford is a town in Hartford County on the east bank of the Connecticut River, directly across from the city of Hartford. It belongs to the Capitol Planning Region and covers 18.7 square miles, of which 0.73 is water.

The town includes the neighborhoods of Burnside, Hockanum and Mayberry Village, and the Census Bureau counted 51,045 residents in 2020. The town sits at an elevation of about 49 feet, close to the river, so drainage and basement moisture are worth checking before a sale.

East Hartford was incorporated as a separate town in October 1783. Manchester split off from it in 1823, and the town adopted a charter with a Town Council form of government in 1929.

sections.h2: What is the history behind East Hartford's housing?
sections.html:
East Hartford was farmland first and a factory town second, and its housing follows that order. Before 1929 the economy was mostly agricultural, with tobacco as the main crop.

That changed in 1929 when Frederick Rentschler of Pratt & Whitney moved production from Hartford to a site of about 1,100 acres in East Hartford. The grounds included Rentschler Field, a small airport used from 1931 to 1999. United Technologies donated the land to the State of Connecticut in 1999, and a stadium that seats 40,000 now stands there as the home field of the UConn football team.

The census count tells the story. The town grew from 17,125 people in 1930 to 57,583 in 1970, then slipped to about 50,000 by 1990 and has stayed close to 51,000 since 2010. Most of that growth came between 1930 and 1970, so sellers should expect buyers to ask about the age of the roof, wiring and heating system.

sections.h2: What does East Hartford's climate mean for a house?
sections.html:
East Hartford has cold winters and warm, humid summers, with about 50 inches of precipitation a year. These are the 1991 to 2020 normals for the town.

MeasureEast Hartford figure
January daily average temperature27.9 °F
July daily average temperature74.5 °F
Average July daily high84.2 °F
Average annual precipitation50.22 inches
Wettest months on averageOctober, December, June and August, each about 4.6 to 4.8 inches

Rain falls in every month, which keeps roofs, gutters and foundation drainage in constant use. A deferred roof or a wet basement is something an inspector will note on any sale that goes through a traditional listing.

sections.h2: Which employers and institutions shape East Hartford?
sections.html:
Pratt & Whitney, the aerospace engine maker, has its headquarters at 400 Main Street in East Hartford and takes up a large share of the town's land. The company's plant once employed tens of thousands of people, and the town's economy still tracks its fortunes.

Other landmarks include a Coca-Cola bottling plant on Main Street, industrial and office parks, and Goodwin University. Great River Park runs along the Connecticut River and Wickham Park, shared with Manchester, has gardens, ponds and a popular sledding hill.

The public schools run through East Hartford Public Schools, which includes East Hartford High School and the Connecticut International Baccalaureate Academy.

Because one employer has such a large footprint, local housing demand can follow its hiring cycles. Ask a local professional how a recent change at the plant affects buyers in your part of town.

sections.h2: What utilities serve an East Hartford house?
sections.html:
Most East Hartford homes use the same set of utilities, and each one appears on a final bill at closing. Knowing the providers helps you schedule transfers and get final readings.

  • Electricity: Eversource Energy
  • Water: the Metropolitan District Commission
  • Natural gas: Connecticut Natural Gas
  • Phone and fiber internet: Frontier Communications
  • Cable television and internet: Comcast

An unpaid water or sewer balance can follow the property, so request final readings and pay open balances before the closing date.

sections.h2: When are East Hartford property taxes due?
sections.html:
East Hartford's 2025 Grand List tax bills had a first installment due July 1, 2026, and the last day to pay without penalty was August 3, 2026. The tax collector accepts online payments, mail and the drop box outside Town Hall, and takes USPS postmarks outside business hours.

ItemEast Hartford detail

Delinquent accounts coded TaxServPay TaxServ directly, (860) 724-9100

The tax collector's page covers only the first installment, so ask the office for the second installment date and the current mill rate. Delinquent motor vehicle or personal property tax can go to a state marshal under a warrant, and the collector explains the process on its page.

sections.h2: What does selling a house in East Hartford involve at the state level?
sections.html:
The seller or the seller's attorney files Connecticut's real estate conveyance tax return when the deed is recorded, and tax applies once the price reaches $2,000 unless the transfer is exempt. East Hartford is town code 043 on the state's list.

The state exemptions most relevant to a house sale include:

  • A transfer between spouses.
  • A deed in lieu of foreclosure on a principal residence.
  • A principal residence sold for less than the mortgages and priority tax or sewer liens against it.
  • A principal residence with a crumbling foundation from pyrrhotite, after a professional engineer's written evaluation.

Each exemption needs the right code on the return. Your closing attorney can confirm whether one applies.

sections.h2: What should an East Hartford seller check before choosing how to sell?
sections.html:
Start with the paperwork and the property, because both set the timeline. A short checklist keeps surprises out of the closing week.

  • Confirm your tax balance with the tax office at (860) 291-7257 or Tax@easthartfordct.gov.
  • Ask the assessor how your property is classified and what its assessed value is.
  • Gather any lease, permit or repair records you have for the house.
  • Collect the utility account names so final readings can be requested.
  • List any liens, judgments or an unpaid mortgage balance that must be cleared at closing.

If the house came to you through an estate, add the probate paperwork to the pile. A title company will want to see who has authority to sign the deed.

sections.h2: What do East Hartford sellers usually face, and how does a cash sale work?
sections.html:
East Hartford sellers often hold a mid-century house that needs updates, a multi-unit property, an inherited house, or a mortgage in arrears, and a cash sale avoids the repair and showing steps.

  • You share the address, condition and your timeline with us.
  • We review the facts and make an offer for the house as it is.
  • If you agree, a title company or attorney prepares the deed and files the state tax return.
  • Liens and unpaid taxes are paid from the proceeds at closing.

We do not set a price before reviewing the property. You can compare any offer with a listing and decide.

faqs.q: What county is East Hartford in?
faqs.a: East Hartford is in Hartford County, Connecticut, on the east side of the Connecticut River across from the city of Hartford.

faqs.q: When are East Hartford property taxes due?
faqs.a: The first installment of the 2025 Grand List bills was due July 1, 2026, with August 3, 2026 as the last day to pay without penalty. Ask the tax collector for the second installment date.

faqs.q: Who provides electricity and water in East Hartford?
faqs.a: Eversource supplies electricity and the Metropolitan District Commission supplies water. Connecticut Natural Gas provides natural gas.

faqs.q: Does East Hartford have a state conveyance tax when I sell?
faqs.a: Yes, Connecticut's conveyance tax return is filed when the deed is recorded, and tax is due on prices of $2,000 or more unless an exemption applies. Your closing attorney can work out the amount.

faqs.q: Can I sell an East Hartford house that needs repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash buyer can purchase a house as it stands, so you do not have to repair or clean it first.

faqs.q: What if my East Hartford taxes are overdue?
faqs.a: Overdue taxes are paid from your sale proceeds at closing. Some delinquent accounts are with TaxServ, and you can call the tax office to confirm the balance.
